beginner.stem: How many protons does a Lutetium atom have? (That number is also its place on the table.)
beginner.explanation: Lutetium is element 71. A neutral atom has 71 protons and 71 electrons.

beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Lutetium?

beginner.stem: Which history line belongs to Lutetium?

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Lutetium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: Around 1907, three chemists each pulled the last rare earth out of ytterbia, and the question of who arrived first became its own dispute.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Lutetium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: The name that won the dispute looks back to Roman Paris, a city label chosen by the chemist whose word the official tables kept.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Lutetium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: A second name circulated in German writings for years, and then the official tables closed the contest in favor of the Paris label.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Lutetium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: With this box filled, the rare-earth row was complete, and a filled electron shell started an argument about where the element belongs.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Lutetium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: The parent earth had already been named and filed, and the last lanthanide was still inside it, waiting on a finer separation.
